projects.title: Turnkeep
projects.descriptor: A printed character case with a digital companion
projects.summary: I designed Turnkeep to put dice, a character display and the things I reach for during a tabletop game into one printed case. The physical prototype sits alongside an open design: editable CAD, printable parts, firmware and build instructions that other makers can adapt. The case is taking shape on the workbench; phone import and transfer are still simulated in the public demo.

projects.title: Reggio projects
projects.descriptor: 15 years of learning through materials and making
projects.summary: For 15 years, I have designed and co-facilitated Reggio-inspired investigations with children in Bangkok, thinking through materials. A terrarium becomes a way to explore sensors; a drawing becomes a circuit or moving machine; a Year 6 AI sprint becomes a chance to question a digital design. My contribution is to prepare the conditions, introduce tools and document how ideas change. The work here belongs to a dialogue between children, educators and the things they make.

projects.title: Padlano
projects.descriptor: Padel rotations, scoring and leagues from one phone
projects.summary: I built Padlano for the organising that happens between games of padel. From one phone, it creates Americano rotations, records scores and ranks players by average points when someone sits out. Players can use it without an account, keep a session on their device or choose to share sessions and leagues. The notebook and electronics shown here belong to a related scoring-device experiment; the web app is live.

projects.title: A school for making
projects.descriptor: An alternative middle school & community maker space
projects.role: Learning model, programme and spatial concept
projects.summary: I am developing an alternative middle school and community maker space around shared workshops, where young people investigate questions by designing, building and testing things. My work connects the learning programme with the tools, materials and spaces it needs. The woodshop and fablab renders explore how hand tools, digital fabrication and shared worktables could support that learning; the diagrams show the inquiry cycle behind it. These are concept visualisations for a school in development.

projects.title: ELC Portal
projects.descriptor: Activities, events and calendars in one family portal
projects.role: Family experience design and web development
projects.summary: I designed and built ELC Portal around a parent's practical questions: what is happening, what can my child join, and where do I go next? It brings school activities, events, calendars and useful information into one family-facing website, with links to the existing registration systems. My work joins school operations with interface design: organising the information and building a consistent route through it. The screenshots show the public activities and calendar pages.

projects.title: Pomodoist
projects.descriptor: A physical focus timer connected to Todoist
projects.summary: I made Pomodoist to keep one task and a focus timer on a small screen beside me. It connects today’s Todoist tasks with a Pomodoro timer, using the device’s own buttons or touch controls. The photographs show the electronics and an enclosed prototype; the separate interface references show the focus and task-selection screens. This is the dedicated desk object, while my wider ESP32 work develops the software it can share with other devices.

projects.title: Project dashboard
projects.descriptor: A project-management tool in a single HTML file
projects.role: Dashboard design, development and public template
projects.summary: I turned a tool from my own project-management work into a single HTML file that other people can adapt and host. The dashboard keeps priorities, completion and weekly progress notes together, with browser storage and an optional shareable view. There is no server to set up for the basic version. The public demo uses sample projects, and the source includes instructions for making it your own.

projects.title: ESP32 experiments
projects.descriptor: TrevOS: a shared foundation for small devices
projects.role: Board integration, firmware and interface experiments
projects.summary: I am building TrevOS, a shared launcher and software foundation for my ESP32 devices. A timer, a padel scoreboard and a desk display can reuse app logic while each board supplies its own screen and controls. This collection shows the work underneath individual products: board experiments, interface sketches and a saved launcher simulation. The aim is to carry what I learn from one device into the next, instead of starting again with every screen.

projects.title: Second Brain Builder
projects.descriptor: Guided questions that become a personal AI workspace
projects.role: Question flow, system design and development
projects.summary: I made Second Brain Builder to turn the structure of my own knowledge system into a starting point for someone else. A personalised question flow asks how they work, plan and keep track of things, then produces a plain-text blueprint for an AI-assisted workspace. Each journey is prepared for its recipient. The public page is the entry point to those individual builds; the source shows how the builder works.

projects.title: Trips

projects.summary: I build small apps for friends and loved ones around something we want to do together. projects.title: Bodybrain
projects.descriptor: Training, nutrition, recovery and bloodwork in context
projects.role: Data system, product thesis and coaching workflow
projects.summary: Bodybrain began as a way to read my training, nutrition and recovery together, instead of opening separate apps and guessing how the pieces connect. I am developing that personal data system into a coaching platform: bringing context to a conversation, agreeing a plan and adjusting it as someone’s life changes. MacroFactor, InBody, Hevy, Google Fit and bloodwork show the kinds of information I want to connect. The screens here are illustrative; the coaching platform is in active development.

projects.title: Custom Media Databank
projects.descriptor: Bringing learning documentation back into use
projects.role: Extraction pipeline, media library and editorial workflow
projects.summary: I built Custom Media Databank to bring the best photographs, artwork and quotes out of project learning publications at a design-focused, Reggio-inspired school. It turns finished PDFs into a searchable editorial library, with source references, duplicate handling and quality flags, so strong material can be found again for publications and social media. Security and children’s safety shape the workflow: access stays behind institutional authentication, and attribution and reuse need human review. The examples here are fictional and anonymised.
